evidence.quote: You can grant access using either Azure RBAC or Key Vault access policies.
Assign the Reader role so Atlas can read Key Vault metadata.
You can also use a custom role, as long as it grants equivalent key permissions.
Access to a key vault is controlled through two interfaces: the control plane and the data plane.
The access controls for the two planes work independently.

statements.statement: Atlas supports Azure RBAC or Key Vault access policies.
The RBAC instructions assign Reader for vault metadata and Key Vault Crypto User, or an equivalent custom role, for key operations.
Microsoft separates management access from cryptographic data-plane access.
statements.note: Control plane vs data plane, independent.

edits.rationale: MongoDB's doc supports Azure RBAC or access policies, Reader plus Key Vault Crypto User or an equivalent custom role. Microsoft's Key Vault RBAC guide states the control plane and data plane are separate access-control interfaces that work independently.

edits.old: Short-lived authentication reduces exposure from durable credentials but still requires narrowly scoped authorization. OWASP recommends temporary credentials and least privilege; MongoDB also directs users to scope the service principal's key permissions narrowly. (medium confidence)
edits.new: Short-lived authentication reduces exposure from durable credentials but still requires narrowly scoped authorization. OWASP recommends dynamic secrets (used only as long as needed) and applying least privilege; MongoDB also directs users to scope permissions as narrowly as possible. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/azure-kms-secretless.md ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html

evidence.quote: You should scope permissions as narrowly as possible and grant them using one of the following options:

the Least Privilege principle should be applied.

statements.statement: MongoDB directs users to scope the service principal's key permissions narrowly.
statements.note: Doc says scope permissions as narrowly as possible.

statements.statement: OWASP recommends temporary credentials and least privilege.
statements.note: OWASP recommends least privilege and dynamic secrets; exact 'temporary credentials' wording not found.

edits.rationale: MongoDB says to scope permissions as narrowly as possible. OWASP's cheat sheet recommends least privilege and describes dynamic secrets as reducing leakage, but it does not literally say 'temporary credentials' are recommended, so the wording is adjusted. The first sentence is the pack's own synthesis.

edits.old: Unversioned Key Vault key URIs are supported and resolve to the latest enabled key version, reducing the need to update configuration after key rotation. (high confidence)
edits.new: Atlas accepts Key Vault key identifiers without a version, and MongoDB recommends omitting the version so the key resolves automatically to the latest version. Microsoft advises using versionless key URIs so services refresh to the latest key version after rotation. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/security/azure-kms-secretless.md ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/keys/how-to-configure-key-rotation

evidence.quote: You may append `/{object-version}`. However, we recommend you omit the version to enable automatic resolution to the latest version.
Target services should use versionless key URI to automatically refresh to the latest version of the key.
